findings.body:
**Target:** R1/R3 and T1-T3
**Issue:** FLOW_COMMANDS.args contains option token names, while placeholders and descriptions currently exist only in raw help text parsed by command-registry.flowOptions(). The spec forbids help reverse-parsing but does not identify where the required CommandOption description, placeholder, alias, kind, and row summary values come from.
**Required change:** Specify the concrete FLOW_COMMANDS or CommandDefinition field/factory that owns structured option and summary metadata, including common guard/runtime options, and state that raw help remains prose rather than an authority.
**Why blocking:** Without that source, implementation must either retain the forbidden reverse parser or create an undocumented parallel authority, and tests have no stable expected display contract.
findings.evidence: The immutable spec bans help reverse-parsing and requires structured option metadata, but does not identify the concrete FLOW_COMMANDS or CommandDefinition field/factory that owns those values; the authority must be named in the requirement text.
findings.issue: FLOW_COMMANDS.args contains option token names, while placeholders and descriptions currently exist only in raw help text parsed by command-registry.flowOptions(). The spec forbids help reverse-parsing but does not identify where the required CommandOption description, placeholder, alias, kind, and row summary values come from.
findings.requiredChange: Specify the concrete FLOW_COMMANDS or CommandDefinition field/factory that owns structured option and summary metadata, including common guard/runtime options, and state that raw help remains prose rather than an authority.
findings.title: Structured option display metadata has no declared authority
findings.whyBlocking: Without that source, implementation must either retain the forbidden reverse parser or create an undocumented parallel authority, and tests have no stable expected display contract.

findings.body:
**Target:** R3/T3: routed leaf --help
**Issue:** The current dispatcher returns entry.help directly when help is requested; flow.js uses that dispatcher path for leaf help. CommandDefinition.renderHelp() only renders group subcommands, and the spec does not identify the integration point that replaces the raw leaf help with projected Usage/Options rows.
**Required change:** Name the routed leaf integration point—such as the dispatcher help shortcut calling a shared leaf renderer—and define how raw prose, locale data, and projected options are combined.
**Why blocking:** Updating only CommandDefinition/group rendering leaves commands such as flow run abort --help on the old raw help, so parser/help parity is not achieved.
findings.evidence: The immutable R3 contract specifies projected leaf options but does not name the dispatcher help shortcut or shared leaf renderer that replaces the current raw entry.help path.

findings.title: Leaf help is not wired to the projected renderer
findings.whyBlocking: Updating only CommandDefinition/group rendering leaves commands such as flow run abort --help on the old raw help, so parser/help parity is not achieved.

findings.body:
**Target:** R7 and src/lib/command-registry.js query projection
**Issue:** FLOW_COMMANDS.query is currently included in flowSubcommands, coreCommandRegistry metadata, routePaths/helpPaths, and the public sennel help flow query route. R7 says query must not appear in CommandDefinition projection but provides no replacement for that existing help/catalog behavior.
**Required change:** State that query is excluded only from routed option/group/inventory projections while its independent CommandDefinition metadata route remains, or specify and test a replacement owner for sennel help flow query and catalog listing.
**Why blocking:** Literal removal from CommandDefinition changes an existing public help route, while query integration tests do not cover that regression.
findings.evidence: The immutable R7 text excludes query from routed projections, while the existing public flow query metadata route is retained elsewhere in the stated context; the required exclusion boundary and preserved owner are not explicit.

findings.body:
**Target:** R1/R4/T4-T5; src/lib/namespace-dispatcher.js and src/help.js
**Issue:** CommandDefinition.renderHelp() is also used by NamespaceDispatcher for docs, check, metrics, spec, and hook namespaces, while CommandDefinition.metadata()/help rendering serves all core and plugin help. The spec does not define an opt-in boundary for the new Flow-specific structured renderer or preservation of these non-flow surfaces.
**Required change:** Explicitly scope the new projection/renderer to routed Flow definitions and preserve existing non-flow NamespaceDispatcher/help behavior, or include those consumers and their regressions in scope.
**Why blocking:** A global CommandDefinition change can alter or break unrelated namespace help while the proposed Flow-focused tests would not detect it.
findings.evidence: The immutable R1/R4 requirements describe shared CommandDefinition and Flow projections but do not state an opt-in boundary for routed Flow definitions or preservation of non-flow namespace help consumers.

The spec does not define an opt-in boundary for the new Flow-specific structured renderer or preservation of these non-flow surfaces.
findings.requiredChange: Explicitly scope the new projection/renderer to routed Flow definitions and preserve existing non-flow NamespaceDispatcher/help behavior, or include those consumers and their regressions in scope.
findings.title: Shared CommandDefinition consumers are outside the stated flow scope
findings.whyBlocking: A global CommandDefinition change can alter or break unrelated namespace help while the proposed Flow-focused tests would not detect it.
